$comment: §15.5's rollout, as data. canary.py reads this; deploy.yml reads canary.py.
The ladder is the chapter's, verbatim: 5, 25, 50, 100, ten minutes each.
It is NOT trimmed to what a three-replica deployment can express, and that
is the point of tolerance.weightOvershootPoints being zero — with three
stable pods a single canary already serves 25%, and a plan that silently
accepted that would have written 5% while shipping five times the blast
radius. `canary.py plan` refuses instead and names the stable replica
count the step needs (ADR-022).
That count is 19, and the charts already permit it: §15.3's
autoscaling.maxReplicas is 20 on the service charts, exactly 19
stable plus one canary. The gateway's is 30, so there the 19 is what the
weight costs rather than all the chart allows.
The smallest configuration in which 5% is expressible is the largest one
the chart allows, and neither number was chosen with the other in mind.
errorRate and latencyP99Seconds are §13.6's alert thresholds and are
asserted equal to them by canary.py check 3, read out of
platform-alerts.yaml rather than restated here. A canary tuned looser
than the alert promotes a release and then pages about it.
minimumRequests is 1/errorRate and is derived rather than picked: below
a hundred requests a single failure is more than one per cent, so the
threshold cannot be expressed at all and a green analysis is arithmetic
rather than evidence.
The two floors exist because a ratio between small numbers is noise. A
baseline of 0.0001 against a canary of 0.0004 is four times worse and is
two requests.
What a workload can be judged on, and which absolute thresholds each
signal is held to (ADR-047). Every signal is also compared with the
stable track on both errorRate and latencyP99Seconds, which needs no
alert to own a number. A workload declares the signals it receives, and
check 9 holds a service that registers a consumer or a saga to
declaring consume or saga, or arguing why not.
PromQL, with three substitutions read_prometheus makes: $SERVICE is the
workload's serviceName, $TRACK is stable or canary, and $WINDOW is the
step's dwell. The window equals the dwell because a rate over the dwell
read at its end is §15.5's watch.
deployment_track is the resource attribute ADR-022 adds; service_version
is not a discriminator, because every build reports the same one.
The or vector(0) on each error-rate numerator is what lets a clean
canary promote: a canary with no failures matches no numerator series,
and PromQL carries the empty vector through the division. Only the
numerator is coalesced, because an empty denominator is no traffic at
all, which requests and minimumRequests judge.
http_route excludes the probe routes Common.Web maps (§13.5), because
the chart's probes alone pass minimumRequests inside one dwell; check
10 holds the pattern to every MapHealthChecks route in src/.

queries.errorRate: (sum(rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{service_name="$SERVICE", deployment_track="$TRACK", http_route!~"/health/.*", http_response_status_code=~"5.."}[$WINDOW])) or vector(0)) / sum(rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{service_name="$SERVICE", deployment_track="$TRACK", http_route!~"/health/.*"}[$WINDOW]))

$comment: MassTransit's own consume instruments, from the meter Common.Web
registers: consume attempts, the faulted ones, and their duration.
The names are the OTLP-to-Prometheus spelling of the instrument and
its unit, ea on the counters and ms on the histogram, so the p99 is
divided back into seconds; canary.py's EXPORTED_SERIES holds each
spelling to the MassTransit version it was read from.
Only errorRate is absolute: it is §13.6's error threshold, and no
alert owns a consume-duration number, so duration is judged against
the stable track alone (ADR-047). A message has no route, so these
carry no route selector.
MassTransit's saga instruments, which count a state machine's messages
apart from the consume ones, so a saga faulting on every message leaves
consume clean. Judged on the same terms as consume, and on its own
minimumRequests (ADR-047).
serviceName is what the process emits and chart is what Helm installs,
and they are different strings for the same thing. Check 4 asserts the
first against the solution's own entry assemblies and the second against
deploy/helm, because a query spelled from the deployment's vocabulary
matches no series — and an empty result rolls every canary back, so the
mistake produces a rollout that can only ever fail.

catalog-api.consumeExemption: Catalog's one consumer is the stock-level projection, fed at a rate Inventory's traffic sets rather than Catalog's, so a canary's share of it cannot be relied on to reach minimumRequests in a dwell and a declared consume signal would roll healthy releases back for quiet. A projection that faults is already loud: it retries and then lands in the error queue §13.6 pages on, and the reads it serves are judged by the http signal.
